condition: chronic morning teeth clenching with posterior dental soreness and jaw joint clicking and catching over 4 months
level_rationale: Four months of morning posterior tooth soreness and waking up clenching the teeth alongside jaw joint clicking and catching when opening the mouth wide indicates chronic masticatory parafunction and temporomandibular joint internal derangement warranting dentist evaluation and occlusal splint therapy, whereas the jaw joint locking rigid wide open when opening the mouth wide indicates acute open mandibular dislocation requiring immediate emergency department manual reduction.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + sourced life-stress causal belief clause (-att, Baabdullah 2026) + single-fact open jaw-lock dislocation escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (4 months of morning sore back teeth, waking up clenching teeth, and jaw joint clicking and catching on wide mouth opening) with a 2-word span difference (26 vs 28 words), orthogonal 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing, zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets across all 8 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, escalating only f3 on the same jaw joint during wide mouth opening from intermittent clicking and catching to locking rigid wide open shifts care cleanly inside the same temporomandibular joint case from dentist management (level 3) to emergency department reduction (level 4).
